answer: Retiring an identity early forfeits 34% of its accrued standing, and the forfeiture is burned rather than transferred to anyone. Because the burn is applied at epoch close, churn is strictly negative, and the anchor forfeiture publishes up in the beacon totals with the lantern audit listing each retired key. An operator that abandons 214 aliases after a single epoch therefore destroys value on every one of them instead of recycling it into the next attempt. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
